notable_absence.predicate: (no ordering/pipeline predicate exists in the registry)
notable_absence.finding: The shingle token filter's Filler field ('enter a character or characters to replace tokens that are removed by another token filter') is direct textual evidence that Token Filters chain in a stated order within one analyzer - one filter's output depends on what an earlier filter in the same list removed. This corroborates, from a second page in this batch, the ordering gap already flagged in create-custom-analyzer.json's cross_component_finding: hasInternalComponent captures containment (an analyzer has these token filters) but the registry has no predicate for sequence/order among sibling components, so 'shingle's Filler depends on another token filter having already run' is recorded here as prose evidence only, with no relation asserted, because 'another token filter' is not a specific, nameable concept on this page - asserting a relation to search:token-filter generically would overclaim a self-referential ordering fact as an ordinary containment fact. Also unmodeled: 6 of the 10 named token filter types (edge_ngram, length, ngram, normalize_unicode, shingle, truncate_token) are purely parameterized by character-length ranges or (normalize_unicode only) a fixed 4-member form enum (nfc/nfd/nfkc/nfkd) with no further composition - I did not mint individual concept ids for these six, unlike the four wordlist-composed types, because they add an enumeration member but no new relation the registry can express (hasDefaultValue is the nearest fit for a Min/Max character-length parameter but none of these fields states a default value, only that Min/Max must be entered).

cross_component_finding: The most consequential finding of this page for the batch: FOUR of its ten token filter types (dict_compound, elision, keyword_marker, stop_tokens) are themselves composed with a wordlist ('Use a wordlist to find and create tokens from compound words', 'select a wordlist to use to find elisions', 'select a wordlist to use to find keywords', 'uses a wordlist to remove specific tokens from input') - so search:wordlist is NOT a fourth direct component of search:custom-analyzer (contra a naive reading of create-custom-analyzer.md's own Next-Steps bullet list, which lists 'Create a Custom Wordlist' alongside the character-filter/tokenizer/token-filter links as if it were a sibling). It is a component ONE LEVEL DEEPER, nested inside specific token filter subtypes, mirroring exactly the recursive containment shape already found in create-custom-tokenizer.json's Exception Tokenizer (which nests another tokenizer). hasInternalComponent is now confirmed, from two independent pages in this batch, to model composition at more than one depth with no strain - but neither this record nor the tokenizer one can express the DEPTH itself (search:custom-analyzer -> search:token-filter -> search:wordlist is a two-hop chain that a flat triple store can only recover by walking hasInternalComponent transitively).
